subject.title: fix(gateway): require shared secret for tailscale serve auth

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `gateway.auth.requireTailscaleSharedSecret` as the permanent opt-in contract for composing Tailscale Serve identity with token/password auth and rotating sessions when that policy changes?
rationale: The implementation is plausible and bounded, but adding a new authentication policy knob and defining its upgrade/session semantics is a security and product contract that cannot be accepted from tests alone.

options.title: Approve after proof and rebase
options.body: Approve this layered-auth contract, require a clean rebase plus current-head running-Gateway/Tailscale proof, then re-review the exact merge result.

options.title: Narrow to awareness only
options.body: Decline the new config surface and retain the existing Tailscale trust model while improving warnings and documentation instead.

options.title: Accept harness proof
options.body: Approve the contract after conflict resolution while explicitly accepting the absence of final-head live Tailscale-daemon proof.

recommendation.title: Approve after proof and rebase
recommendation.body: Approve this layered-auth contract, require a clean rebase plus current-head running-Gateway/Tailscale proof, then re-review the exact merge result.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest concrete history is the recent merged Gateway credential-rotation work, where this person merged the adjacent auth/session behavior.
